3R replication script (analysis.R)

How to replicate: save the block below as analysis.R, place cleaned.csv (in the export bundle) beside it, then run Rscript analysis.R. The script prints every table shown in the app; the app's numbers were verified byte-for-byte against native R output. Package citations are in section 6.
# Reproducible analysis script generated by Telos
# Run from the folder holding cleaned.csv. Uncomment install.packages() the first time.
# install.packages(c("modelsummary", "car", "effectsize", "ggplot2"))
library(modelsummary)
library(car)
library(effectsize)
library(ggplot2)
d <- read.csv("cleaned.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
d[["gender"]] <- factor(d[["gender"]])

# === 01 · Independent t-test ===
itt <- data.frame(score = d[["exam_score"]], g = factor(d[["gender"]]))
print(datasummary_balance(~g, data = itt, dinm = FALSE))  # Table 1 (Arel-Bundock datasummary)
res <- t.test(d[["exam_score"]] ~ factor(d[["gender"]]), var.equal = FALSE, conf.level = 0.95, alternative = "two.sided")
print(res)
print(car::leveneTest(score ~ g, data = itt, center = median))
print(effectsize::cohens_d(score ~ g, data = itt, pooled_sd = TRUE))
print(ggplot(itt, aes(g, score)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#9cc2ec", colour = "#0c447c") + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL))

LaTeX source (report.tex)
\documentclass{article}

\usepackage[T1]{fontenc}

\usepackage{booktabs,graphicx,siunitx}

\begin{document}

\section{Independent t-test}

\begin{tabular}{lllll}
\toprule
Group & N & Mean & Std. Dev. & SE \\
\midrule
Female & 120 & 65.69 & 8.31 & 0.76 \\
Male & 120 & 65.44 & 8.03 & 0.73 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\begin{tabular}{lllllll}
\toprule
Contrast & t & df & p & Mdiff & 95\% CI & Cohen's d [95\% CI] \\
\midrule
Female $-$ Male & 0.24 & 237.73 & .810 & 0.25 & [$-$1.82, 2.33] & 0.03 [$-$0.22, 0.28] \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\includegraphics{figures/01_independent-t-test/figure_boxplot.png}

Asks whether two groups' averages differ by more than chance. Look at p: below alpha (e.g. 0.05) means significant. The mean difference and 95\% CI show the size and precision of the gap; Cohen's d gives effect size (\textasciitilde{}0.2 small, 0.5 medium, 0.8 large). A large p means no significant difference was detected - not that the group means are equal.

An independent-samples t-test compared Female (M=65.7, SD=8.3) and Male (M=65.4, SD=8.0), t(237.73)=0.24, p = .810, d=0.03 [$-$0.22, 0.28].

Statistical basis: Independent-samples t-test (pooled variance) (Student (1908). "The probable error of a mean." Biometrika, 6(1), 1-25.); Welch's correction (unequal variances, the app's default) (Welch, B. L. (1947). "The generalization of Student's problem when several different population variances are involved." Biometrika, 34(1-2), 28-35.); Cohen's d effect-size benchmarks (.2/.5/.8) (Cohen, J. (1988). Statistical Power Analysis for the Behavioral Sciences (2nd ed.). Routledge.); Levene's test for equal variances (Brown-Forsythe median-centered variant) (Levene, H. (1960). "Robust tests for equality of variances." In I. Olkin (Ed.), Contributions to Probability and Statistics (pp. 278-292). Stanford University Press.); Brown-Forsythe median-centered variant of the homogeneity-of-variance test (Brown, M. B., Forsythe, A. B. (1974). "Robust tests for the equality of variances." Journal of the American Statistical Association, 69(346), 364-367.).

Harness README
# 05 · Independent t-test

**Question:** do two groups' means differ?

**Scenario:** Campus study: do male and female students' exam scores differ (the honest null)?

## Input configuration

- **Dataset:** `campus-study.csv`
- **Configure-data:** app defaults (auto-detected types/levels)
- **Options:** equal variance OFF → Welch (drawn default); two-tailed; α 0.05; 95% CI

**Role assignments** (drag column → slot):

| Column | Role slot |
|---|---|
| `exam_score` | outcome |
| `gender` | group |
